Section 2 · Your account

Audit of your live ads & landing page

Read from your live creatives in the Transparency Center and your landing pages on locksmiths247.ie. What's working, what's leaking Quality Score, and what competitors are doing that you aren't.

What's already good

  • Volume and structure: 33 live creatives with per-area ads (“Swords Locksmiths247™”, “Locksmiths247™ Tallaght”) and a separate auto locksmith theme — most rivals run one generic campaign.
  • Image assets on several ads (van + branded alarm-box shots) — very few locksmith advertisers in Dublin use these; they earn extra SERP real estate.
  • Offer language: “Quotes & Fixed Charges”, “Dispatched in 15min” — concrete and credible.
  • Landing page trust stack: PSA licence #00709 on-page, Garda-vetted line, named Lynch team with photos, freephone 1800 47 47 47 clickable everywhere, physical shop at 20 Upper Abbey Street.

What's leaking money

  • Fix “Lock Smith Service At DoorStep” — “Lock Smith” as two words and “DoorStep” mid-caps reads mistyped, and “locksmith” as one word is what Google matches against. It also breaks your own ™ branding. One weak headline drags CTR on every ad it rotates into.
  • Fix Truncated headline: “Lock Smith Service At DoorStep - Best Price Guar…” — the second headline exceeds its slot. Keep each headline ≤30 characters so “Best Price Guarantee” actually renders.
  • Improve Display paths: your ads show locksmiths247.ie/free_call_out/open_24hrs — underscores look technical. Display paths are free ad copy: use /Dublin/24-7-Callout or /Tallaght/Emergency.
  • Improve No prices in copy: your own site says average labour €70, but no creative leads with a number. Locksmiths 365 advertise “Only €90” organically; in ads, a concrete “Lockouts from €70 — Price Agreed First” beats every vague “affordable prices” in the auction.
  • Fix Your Google Business Profile is your weakest asset: “Locksmiths 247 - Locksmith Dublin” shows 4.1★ — the lowest of any major player (Dyno 4.8, Lockman 4.9, Baggot 4.7, Nokego 4.9). It cost you the map pack: you appear top-5 in only one of the eleven mapped local queries. The map pack sits above your paid slot on “near me” searches — you are paying for clicks while the pack takes the calls.
  • Improve Landing page mismatches: the Swords ad lands on the generic 24-hr page rather than a Swords page, and the quote form asks for vehicle details on non-auto enquiries. Tighter ad-to-page match raises Quality Score and lowers your CPC for free.

Section 5 · Battle plan

How to out-rank and out-bid them

1 · Fix the map pack before spending another euro on “near me”

Your 4.1★ profile is the single most expensive number in your business: the pack outranks your paid slot on emergency searches, and Google feeds profile quality into local ad serving too (your location assets inherit it). Target: 4.6★+ and +10 reviews per month.

  • SMS/WhatsApp the review link the moment the van door closes — the Lynch team's named, face-on branding is perfect for “please mention Ken/Barry/Cliff in your review”. Aim at your last 200 satisfied jobs to dilute the old low ratings.
  • Reply to every existing 1–3★ review, factually and calmly — replies are ranking signals and read by the next caller.
  • Fill every GBP field: primary category Locksmith, secondary Emergency locksmith service; services list per suburb; photos of vans, shopfront, team; Q&A seeded with “do you charge a call-out fee?”.
  • Your Abbey Street shop is a genuine advantage — most rivals are service-area-only profiles. Post weekly (jobs done in named suburbs) to keep the profile active.

2 · Restructure the account around intent × area

You already have area ads — finish the job. Four intent campaigns (Emergency lockout · Lock change/security · Auto keys · Commercial), each split into tight ad groups per area (city centre, North, South, West, plus the suburbs you already target: Swords, Tallaght, Dundrum, Dún Laoghaire, Blackrock, Rathfarnham). Every ad group: one RSA, area-matched final URL, area name pinned in Headline 1 or 2.

Dayparting: most rivals run small budgets that exhaust by evening; The Lockman is the only always-on heavyweight. Add +20–40% bid adjustments 6pm–2am and weekends, when intent is desperate and auctions thin. Pair with a call-only campaign for “locked out” / “emergency locksmith near me” after-hours — a stressed caller at 1am does not want a website.

3 · Rewrite the weak creatives

Drop-in replacements (all within character limits) — fix the typo ad first:

Emergency · Dublin (RSA headlines to rotate/pin)
H1 (pin): Locksmiths247™ Dublin · H2: Lockouts From €70 — Fixed First · H3: At Your Door In 15–30 Min · H4: PSA Licensed & Garda Vetted · H5: Open Now — 24/7 Callout
Display path: locksmiths247.ie/Dublin/24-7-Callout
D1: Price agreed before we drive. No hidden call-out fees. Freephone 1800 47 47 47. D2: Local Lynch family team, 20+ years in Dublin. Non-destructive entry where possible.

Assets to load on every campaign: call asset (1800 47 47 47), location asset (link the GBP — another reason to fix it), callouts (PSA Licence 00709 · Garda Vetted · Fixed Quotes · Insured), structured snippet (Services: Lockouts, Lock Changes, Car Keys, Safes, Alarms), price asset (Lockout from €70 · Lock change from €89 — use your real floors), and keep the image assets running.

4 · Exploit what the data says about each rival

  • DIALOCK / locksmithservice.ie (~500 ads): the real paid heavyweight — an auto-generated creative farm (per-area call ads, “Call (01) 223 8734”), and the only rival already showing Seller Ratings stars (4.8★, 99 reviews) under its ads. Do not try to match creative volume; match their assets (stars, call-first) and beat them on authenticity — their brand is two years old, yours has a shop and 20 years.
  • The Lockman (45 ads): their whole rotation funnels to one generic emergency page and leans on “24/7” claims. Beat them on specificity: prices, named team, PSA licence, area pages. Don't out-shout — out-trust.
  • A.P. Lock & Safe (26): heritage angle (“since '77”), strong in south suburbs organic. Your counter: speed + fixed pricing; they publish neither.
  • The Slándála network (XL Lock 21 + Emergency Locksmiths 24/7): one operator, multiple lookalike brands, anonymous. Your counter-copy: “A real Dublin shop — visit us on Abbey Street”. Anonymous networks can't match a face and a counter.
  • 24 Hour Locksmith (18): bids your core emergency terms; sole-trader entity. Out-cover them with assets (images, prices, seller ratings) they don't run.
  • Dyno Locks (2 ads): the biggest brand is barely advertising — they're coasting on #1 organic and 4.8★. That's your opening in paid: own the ad slots on their strongest keywords while they sleep.
  • Baggot & Nokego (0 ads, dormant accounts): they own the city-centre pack. When they wake up, your defence is being #1 in ads with better assets already earned.

5 · Measurement & hygiene

  • Your AW-1071771702 tag is live — make sure calls are the primary conversion (call assets + Google forwarding numbers + call-from-website tracking, count calls ≥40s), and move campaigns to Target CPA once you log 30+ call conversions/month.
  • Weekly search-terms mining. Starting negative list: jobs, course, training, apprenticeship, DIY, how to, pick a lock, wiki, free, timpson, cheap (keep “cheap” only if you don't want bargain hunters).
  • Collect Google-syndicated reviews (Trustpilot/Reviews.io) toward Seller Ratings — the star row under ads needs ~100 reviews in 12 months. DIALOCK already shows 4.8★ seller ratings on its ads — until you match it, their ad physically outshines yours in the same auction. This is now table stakes, not a nice-to-have.
  • Budget split to start: 55% emergency · 25% auto keys · 20% area/commercial. Estimated €3–€8 CPC on core emergency terms (industry estimate — verify in Keyword Planner with your own account data).
Method & limitations. Advertiser status, verified entities and creative counts: Google Ads Transparency Center, region Ireland, last 30 days, captured 14 Aug 2026 — Google's own advertiser disclosure data, authoritative for who is advertising and with what creatives, but it does not expose per-keyword ad positions. Live Google.ie ad-slot screenshots could not be captured because Google serves automated-traffic checks to this network; verifying exact ad positions per keyword needs a check from an Irish IP or a rank tracker with an Irish location. Local rankings: captured live from Google Maps with the viewport centred on each area — the closest public proxy for the local pack. Organic listings: compiled from Irish-intent web-index results and cross-checked against the sites; treat ordering as indicative rather than a pixel-accurate Google.ie SERP. All screenshots are unedited captures. CPC figures are labelled industry estimates, not measured data.
